title: unify-stream-resume-handshake-and-backoff-config-across-sdks
author: Sofia Alvarez
description:
Context and motivation:
This PR converges the streaming resume protocol and retry/backoff ergonomics between the Python SDK and the TypeScript/Go SDKs. Over the last quarter we observed divergence in how SDKs attempt 'resume' vs 'restart' logic during transient infra failures and token rotations. The mismatch caused two classes of customer-visible failures: (1) duplicated partial responses after failed reconnects and (2) race conditions when token refreshes overlapped stream reconnects.

Goals:
- Introduce an auth-handshake shim that serializes token refresh vs stream reconnect work to avoid race conditions.
- Standardize the resume token header and ephemeral resume semantics so SDKs behave consistently.
- Add BackoffConfig to expose tunable retry/backoff parameters for Dedicated and customer-managed deployments.
- Preserve public surface with an opt-in legacy flag and migration docs.

What changed (summary):
- StreamSession state machine (sdk/stream/session.py) centralizes connect/resume/teardown and guarantees single-event emission for consumers.
- Auth handshake shim (sdk/auth/handshake.py) uses an in-process asyncio.Lock to serialize refresh/reconnect; introduces ``prepare_stream_auth()`` hook used by stream clients.
- Resume token header standardized to `X-Redwood-Stream-Resume`. Server-side ephemeral token semantics documented in MIGRATION.md.
- BackoffConfig (sdk/backoff/config.py) with defaults aligned across SDKs (initial=30ms, max=8000ms, factor=2.0, jitter=0.15). Can be set via REDWOOD_SDK_BACKOFF env or programmatically.
- Stream.iter_events() yields typed Event objects; legacy_iter=True preserves old generator shapes for backwards compatibility.
- StreamClient.stream_context() context manager added to simplify teardown.
- Tests: updated unit and integration tests (tests/test_stream_resume.py, tests/integration_stream_canary.py). CI integration job includes a flakiness retry wrapper for infra instability.
- Version bumped to 1.8.0.

Testing performed:
- Local unit tests: 140 tests passing.
- Staging integration canary: validated resume across 200 reconnection cycles, zero duplicate events.
- Cross-SDK parity runs with TS/Go: header and backoff parity confirmed.

Backward compatibility and migration notes:
- New resume is default; legacy_iter=True retains prior behavior (deprecated).
- Custom token refresh hooks must adopt ``prepare_stream_auth()`` to avoid long blocking operations during refresh. See MIGRATION.md.

Files changed (high-level):
- sdk/stream/session.py (+220 additions, -32 deletions)
- sdk/auth/handshake.py (+160 additions)
- sdk/backoff/config.py (+98 additions)
- sdk/client.py (+50 additions, -12 deletions)
- tests/test_stream_resume.py (+142 additions, -44 deletions)
- MIGRATION.md (+88 additions)

Review conversation (high level):
- Ethan Park requested clearer separation of responsibilities between StreamSession and StreamClient; moved lifecycle methods into session.
- Maya Chen suggested tightening default backoff for mobile-heavy workloads; we kept defaults conservative and documented tuning.
- Luca Moretti approved after a small rename (prepare_stream_auth -> prepare_stream_auth).
- Author ran a follow-up commit to fix a race in the auth shim discovered in CI and pushed a small test coverage increase.

Merge: squash and merge.

Release notes:
- SDK: Improved streaming resume semantics and auth handshake to prevent duplicate events and token-rotation races. Added BackoffConfig for tuning retry behavior. (1.8.0)
